what: THE MAP'S TRAVEL CLOCK: how fast a journey crosses the map in real time. Hold PLAY on the phone and slide (rule 311, ask 304). WORLD 5, 11/2/26. Mod-friendly: edit the numbers, the map reads this file at boot.
unit: blocks of the map a beat; one beat is 500 ms (120 BPM law). 1 = regular time, one block on every beat.
stepsWhy: Each step is a whole number of blocks a beat, so every block lands on the beat or on an even split of it (2 = eighth notes, 4 = sixteenths). 8x was built and measured and is left out: with only the clock and the steps running it still fell 150 ms behind its slots and moved 8.6 of its 16 blocks a second (a map block costs about 20 ms of work before any drawing), so it cannot stay on the music. The code takes any whole number up to 16; a modder can add 8. The music never speeds up or changes pitch; only how many blocks fit in a beat changes. Every block still pays its own game clock, so a crossing costs the same game hours at every step, only fewer real seconds.
pickWhy: Measured on the demo, upright phone (records/BOHEMIA_WORLD_HOLD_PLAY_SLIDE_THE_SPEED_11_2_26.md): see the record for the crossing times at each step and why this one.
dropWhy: AMENDED 11/4 (rule 398, Paolo: 'these little pop-up events are fucking with my fast speed vibe, if I make it four I have to make it again, it is annoying as fuck'): nothing drops the march to regular time any more. A party met, a fight, a chase, a road event still holds the map while its card is up (PAUSE, rule 44a), and when it closes the march goes on at the speed he had (4x stays 4x). The list is kept, empty, so a modder can put a kind back.
holdWhy: How long a finger stays on PLAY before the slider comes up. A tap is shorter than this and still plays or pauses.
